34	  -> select segment ids -> [(start,end)] (+ stitching padding)

19	## 1. Executive summary
20	
21	The product sits at the intersection of three favorable trends: (a) a fast-growing
22	**sports analytics market** (~USD 5–6B in 2025, ~18–22% CAGR to USD 24–36B by ~2034
23	depending on vendor); (b) a structural shift to **amateur self-recording** on action
24	cameras and phones (action-camera market ~USD 6.5B in 2024, sports the largest
25	segment); and (c) **strong racket-sport participation** — 220M+ badminton players,
26	106M tennis players (2024), and a near-vertical pickleball curve (~19.8M US players in
27	2024, +45.8% YoY).
28	
29	The central tension is the **static-camera constraint**: the tool works best on fixed,
30	full-court amateur footage and *fails* on broadcast/panning footage. This is both a
31	moat (most competitors target team sports / broadcast) and a filter on the addressable
32	user — the customer must already set a camera on a tripod behind the court. That
33	behavior is concentrated in **coaches/academies, clubs, and serious enthusiasts**, not
34	the median casual player.
35	
36	**Recommended beachhead (strongest single):** **badminton coaching academies and
37	serious club/competitive players in India** — a large, rapidly formalizing academy
38	ecosystem (Khelo India tailwind), genuine fixed-angle recording behavior, existing
39	willingness to pay for coaching, an underserved tooling gap (incumbents are
40	team-sports/broadcast), and a direct-but-immature competitor field. The product is
41	*native badminton-first* — a genuine edge here. Secondary: **(2) US/global pickleball
42	players & clubs** (capital-rich, fastest-growing, but SwingVision already strong);
43	**(3) badminton academies/clubs in East/SE Asia + Denmark** (highest density).
44	
45	**Pricing** clusters into hardware-bundled auto-filming (Veo, Trace, Pixellot, Spiideo)
46	and software-only phone AI (SwingVision USD 179.99/yr; BadPro+ pay-per-use). A
47	software-only BYO-camera model undercuts the hardware players; realistic anchors
48	**(estimate): B2C USD 60–180/yr; B2B academy/club USD 300–1,500/yr per location.**
49	
50	**Top risks:** (1) amateurs won't reliably set up a tripod → TAM collapses to
51	coaches/clubs; (2) free/near-free alternatives cap B2C WTP; (3) capture-quality
52	variance is the core failure mode; (4) badminton's strongest markets (India, Indonesia,
53	China) are the most price-sensitive and hardest to bill at Western SaaS prices.

1	# Roadmap — from annotated data to a self-improving, offline rally segmenter
2	
3	This document is the **narrative thread**: how the indexer evolves from an
4	AI-API-dependent prototype into a self-contained tool that learns rally detection
5	from its own commercially-licensed, annotated video corpus. It explains *how we
6	got here*, *why each step matters*, and *how it shapes the final tool*. Decisions
7	are recorded as ADRs in [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md); the scoring mechanics live
8	in [EVALUATION.md](EVALUATION.md).
9	
10	## The thesis
11	
12	The indexer detects badminton rallies in long recordings. Its strongest mode
13	(`yolo_hybrid`) is a two-stage pipeline: cheap **permissive person-detection
14	player-motion** filtering (Stage 1, local — torchvision Faster R-CNN + ByteTrack
15	tracking) followed by **Gemini** semantic refinement (Stage 2, paid API). That
16	works, but it costs money, needs the network, and never improves on its own.
17	
18	> *Naming note:* the `yolo_hybrid` registry key is retained for back-compat, but
19	> AGPL YOLOv8 was removed and replaced with a BSD/MIT-licensed torchvision +
20	> ByteTrack stack — see **ADR-005**. "YOLO" in this doc means the local
21	> player-motion gating stage, not the Ultralytics library.
22	
23	A sibling project, **sports-data-collector**, curates sports videos with
24	per-rally `[start, end)` annotations and a commercial-license flag. The thesis of
25	this roadmap: **use that annotated, commercially-usable data to (1) measure the
26	pipeline objectively and (2) train an offline replacement for the paid Gemini
27	stage** — turning the tool into one that improves as more data is curated, runs
28	air-gapped, and generalizes across sports.
29	
30	Why it matters: it removes the per-run API cost and network dependency, gives us
31	a defensible quality metric instead of eyeballing, and creates a flywheel —
32	more curated matches → a better offline segmenter → better highlights.
33	
34	## The four phases
35	
36	### Phase 1 — Bridge the repos (DONE)
37	A sport-agnostic `curate export` in the collector emits the indexer's `start,end`
38	ground-truth CSVs plus a `manifest.json` pairing each CSV with its video, gated on
39	the `is_commercial` flag. → *Why:* one clean producer/consumer contract that works
40	for all five supported sports (badminton/tennis/cricket/pickleball/table-tennis) alike.
41	See **ADR-002**.
42	
43	### Phase 2 — Acquire full-resolution video (DONE)
44	The corpus was 256×144 (the original crawl used `worstvideo`). The `fetch` command
45	re-acquires every video at **best available resolution (1080p here)**, **in place**
46	(preserving annotations), via **authenticated Firefox Premium cookies** and yt-dlp's
47	`default` client. → *Why:* YOLO/shuttle detection needs real pixels; and the
48	journey surfaced non-obvious traps (SABR streaming → 144p; Chrome DPAPI; rate
49	limiting) now encoded in the tooling. **22/22 fetchable matches are now 1080p.**
50	See **ADR-003**.
51	
52	### Phase 3 — Evaluate + tune (IN PROGRESS)
53	`run_phase3_eval.py` walks the manifest, processes each video, and scores detected
54	rallies against the ground truth — per video and corpus-aggregate (precision/recall/
55	F1, mean IoU, boundary error), for both the `candidates` (raw detector) and `final`
56	(refined) stages. → *Why:* the candidates-vs-final split tells us *where* error
57	lives — a **detection** problem (candidates miss rallies) vs. a **segmentation**
58	problem (candidates catch them, refinement is loose). That diagnosis decides where
59	effort goes, and establishes the baseline any trained model must beat.
60	
61	### Phase 4 — Learn an offline, API-free segmenter (NEXT)
62	Replace the paid Gemini refinement with a **lightweight classifier trained on the
63	rally annotations**, consuming features the pipeline already computes and stores
64	(`candidate_segments.stats`). No external API, no new labeling. → *Why:* this is the
65	payoff — a free, offline, self-improving rally ...
[/external_agent_tool_result]

1	# Platform Architecture — Multi-User "Assistant Coach"
2	
3	**Status:** 📐 Strategy / research — for review. No code yet.
4	**Date:** 2026-06-07 · **Owner:** avidullu
5	
6	**Purpose.** Map the path from today's **single-user, local** tool to a **multi-tenant
7	"assistant coach" platform**: users upload videos, get highlights **stored and
8	browsable by history**, and choose **where their data lives** (Google Drive / cloud
9	bucket / local) and **where the compute runs** (our GPU / their VM). The organizing
10	principle is to **decouple the layers** — identity, ingestion, storage, orchestration,
11	execution/compute, the detection+highlight pipeline, and data-serving — behind small
12	**pluggable interfaces**, reusing the registry pattern the codebase already uses for
13	segmenters/providers/validators/sports/annotations.
14	
15	**Product framing (the north star *and* the v1 line).** This is an **assistant coach**,
16	not just a clipper — but the strategy is **phased and unambiguous about scope**:
17	- **v1 (concrete, near-term):** **rally detection → highlight-reel compilation → per-user
18	  history → a coach/user correction loop that feeds the golden set** ("assistant-coach
19	  *lite*"). Essentially today's pipeline made multi-user — this is the real v1 deliverable.
20	- **Mid-term:** **rich rally/shot semantic metadata** (shot type, rally outcome) and the
21	  **owned video-QA model** (§5A; §6 P4–P5).
22	- **North-star vision (strictly future — *not* v1):** **gait / biomechanics, per-athlete
23	  identifying templates, and deep coaching feedback under a supervising coach** (§6 P6).
24	  Inspiring, but explicitly deferred — and the part that raises the **biometric** privacy
25	  bar (§7).
26	
27	The buyer is the **academy/coach** (beachhead in
28	[`PMF_MARKET_RESEARCH.md`](PMF_MARKET_RESEARCH.md)); **power users self-serve**. Two
29	consequences ripple through the design: (1) the data model keeps an **optional coach →
30	athlete overlay over a generic core** (§4.1) — not baked in; (2) gait/biometrics is
31	**special-category data**, gated and deferred (§7).
32	
33	> **Competitive note (validated by research):** none of Veo / Hudl / SwingVision /
34	> Spiideo offer true BYO-storage or BYO-compute — they're vendor-cloud SaaS
35	> (SwingVision uniquely runs *edge* compute on the user's iPhone). So **"your video,
36	> your storage, your compute"** is a genuine differentiator for privacy-sensitive
37	> academies — and SwingVision proves user-side compute is commercially viable. All four
38	> share the same **teams → athletes → clips** data model, which we adopt (§4).
39	
40	> Scope: this is a **direction-setting doc**. It does not start implementation; the
41	> first infra slice (an async job model) is the on-hold #16 in
42	> [`DEFERRED_HARDENING_PLAN.md`](DEFERRED_HARDENING_PLAN.md). Commercial constraints come
43	> from [`COMMERCIALIZATION.md`](COMMERCIALIZATION.md) (C4 paid-LLM no-train; C12 SaaS
44	> foundations) and `archives/MONETIZATION_AUDIT.md`.
45	
46	## 1. Current state & gaps (what we're evolving from)
47	
48	| Concern | Today | Gap for multi-user |
49	|---|---|---|
50	| Identity / tenancy | none | no users, orgs, auth, or isolation |
51	| Storage | local `filepath` string; output to `output_dir` | no abstraction; can't BYO Drive/bucket; raw video must be on the box |
52	| Data model | `videos` keyed by file **MD5**, `play_segments`, `events`, `candidate_segments` (SQLite) | no owner/athlete link; **highlights aren't a first-class persisted entity** (compile writes a file and returns a path); no per-user history |
53	| Execution | pipeline runs **in-process, synchronously** in `/api/process` | blocks; can't dispatch to a user's VM/GPU; no job status |
54	| Pipeline | **already pluggable** (segmenter/provider/validator/sport/annotation registries) | reuse as-is — this layer is the model for the rest |
55	| API | `/api/process`, `/api/query`, `/api/compile`, `/api/config`; no auth | needs auth, per-tenant scoping, ...
[/external_agent_tool_result]

# Deep audit — sports highlight indexer + collector (2026-06-10)

**How this was produced:** I ramped up per your init notes (handoff → `CODE_MAP.md` → strategy docs read first-hand), then ran an 18-agent workflow — 8 deep auditors with adversarial verification of every critical/high finding. Three auditors (testing, docs-strategy, PMF+web-research) completed fully; **five hit the session rate limit** (resets ~15:50 IST) — engineering-pipeline, eval-methodology, reliability, collector, and technical-docs. Those five are resumable with cached results; say the word after 15:50 and I'll finish the pass. What follows is grounded in the verified two-thirds plus my own first-hand reading.

## 🔴 The headline: `master` is broken right now

[compiler.py](backend/pipeline/stitcher/compiler.py:100) has **seven f-strings that lost their quotes** in the print→logger sweep (commit `7fbbeb0`, 2026-06-07) — lines 100, 104, 156, 160, 181, 191, 213. It's a `SyntaxError`, and since [main.py:28](backend/main.py:28) imports `VideoCompiler` at module level, **`import backend.main` fails — the FastAPI server cannot start and `/api/compile` cannot run.** I reproduced it myself (`py_compile` exit 1), two independent verifier agents confirmed it, and it has survived ~38 commits including merged PRs #58–#61. I've put up a chip (`task_2b7a19d4`) with the exact fix + a smoke-test guard — one click to spin it off.

The deeper lesson is *why* it shipped: the 254-test suite stayed 100% green the whole time because **zero tests import `backend.main`, the compiler, `wasb_hybrid`, `motion`, or any concrete validator — and there is no CI at all** (no `.github/`, nothing invokes `run_all_tests.py`). A one-line `compileall` step would have blocked it.

## Engineering state

The architecture is genuinely good for a project at this stage. The registry/ABC plugin pattern (segmenters/providers/validators/sports/annotations) is consistently applied and is exactly the right seam for the planned Storage/Compute registries; the typed Pydantic config with a legacy `.get()` shim, the `PRAGMA user_version` migration ladder, the detector-runner ABC quarantining the WSL seam, and the never-raises observability layer are all coherent, deliberate engineering. `CODE_MAP.md` is unusually honest — most of the sharp edges (twin-segmenter copy-paste drift, `INSERT OR REPLACE` cascade-delete on re-ingest, silent-empty-vs-error provider returns, `timeout_sec=0` = hang-forever, config shallow-merge) are *documented* footguns rather than unknown ones.

The caveats, evidenced even without the dedicated auditor: the copy-paste twins (`wasb_hybrid`/`tracknet_hybrid`, 191 diff lines) are a live drift surface with zero shared contract test; hardcoded tuned constants are duplicated by copy (`BASELINE`, `TUNED`, paddings) so re-tuning won't propagate; and the compiler bug shows the "hot path" logging sweep was done without even an import check. The eval stack (`metrics`/`calibration`/`eval_partial_labels`/`rally_seq_proto`) is the project's center of gravity and its best-engineered part — honest LOVO, partial-label window restriction, overfit guards — and it's also the best-tested (~115 tests).

## Testing

**Real numbers:** 254 tests / 38 files / ~3.6k LOC, all passing in 19.9s, deterministic, low flake risk (clean `tmp_path` discipline, registries never mutated). Mocks are faithful to real contracts (provider tuple shape, ffprobe bytes, upload→poll→delete lifecycle), and `test_wasb_cache.py` is excellent crash-recovery testing.

**The problem is placement, not quality — coverage is inverted relative to production risk:**
- The *non-default* tracknet twin has 8 tests; the **live** `wasb_hybrid` has 0. `TrackNetRunner` has 21 tests; `WasbRunner` has 1. (A verifier fairly noted this asymmetry is documented in CODE_MAP as deliberate — but the compiler incident shows why "documented" ≠ "safe".)
- No `TestClient`, so all four API endpoints are untested; the 221-line ffmpeg compiler is untested; all six concrete validators are untested — including `pts_continuity`, which **already broke once in production** on HEVC/GDR keyframes per `TEST_RUN_SUMMARY.md`.
- "Fully mocked, runs anywhere" is false: several tests/modules do bare `import cv2`/`numpy` at collection time. The suite is green on your machine because it has cv2/torch installed; on the documented cv2-free container it would *error*, not skip.
- No CI, no conftest, no markers, no coverage measurement. Also note `TEST_RUN_SUMMARY.md` is not a suite summary — it's a May-2026 field diagnosis.

**Cheapest high-value fixes:** a `compileall`/import smoke test, one TestClient test per endpoint, a parametrized contract test across the three hybrids, and a minimal GitHub Actions job. That set would have caught the only critical bug found.

## Reliability (partial — full auditor pending)

From the deferred-hardening plan, CODE_MAP, and collateral evidence: the deliberate deferrals (sync `/api/process`, no auth/tenancy, SQLite single-box) are correctly catalogued in [DEFERRED_HARDENING_PLAN.md](docs/DEFERRED_HARDENING_PLAN.md) with sensible designs. The known-but-worth-restating risks for the async slice: SQLite concurrency under a thread pool, the destructive `add_video` re-ingest cascade, silent-empty provider returns (mitigated by the report rules — a genuinely good design), and the unbounded WSL hang (`timeout_sec=0`). I'd add one *new* reliability item the docs don't carry: **research-artifact fragility** — the n=6 manifest is gitignored and the Roora pickleball/TT labels + trajectories live only in `%TEMP%`, which Windows can clear. Your headline multisport evidence (TT 0.909 / pickleball 0.308) is one disk-cleanup away from existing only in memory files.

## Roadmap/docs inconsistencies (verified, with quotes in the audit output)

The strategy stack is dense and unusually honest, but it has **one-directional drift: decisions ratified in the newest doc were never back-propagated to the most-read docs.**

## PMF — my grounded opinion

The web research **verified your pricing and cost assumptions almost exactly** (SwingVision $179.99/yr; Trace/Veo as documented; Gemini COGS ~$0.30–0.60/hr of video vs PB Vision's *$8/hr* partner API price → fat margin room) — but it **falsified the central beachhead claim**. "Incumbents ignore badminton; India is whitespace" is wrong as of mid-2026: Bangalore specifically is the most contested badminton-AI city anywhere — **Machaxi** ($1.5M, Rainmatter + Prakash Padukone), **VISIST.AI** (70+ Bengaluru academies via the Padukone School), **Game Theory** (Gopichand-backed smart courts that already deliver auto-highlights with court bookings), and **Stupa** ($3.3M, BWF-approved, TT→badminton). None appear in `PMF_MARKET_RESEARCH.md`. The celebrity-academy networks those players own are precisely the distribution a solo, pre-product project lacks.

My honest read:

- **The technical wedge survives, narrowed.** Nobody — including those four — does software-only, rally-precise indexing of a user's *own* full-match footage, and nobody handles **multi-court contamination** in software (the market's only answer is per-court installed hardware at $949–1,533/camera). Your own experiments produced this differentiator: the learned prototype decouples from multi-court (AUC 0.83–0.92) where the heuristic, audio, and spatial gating all provably fail. That + the eval harness is the real moat — exactly as the plan says ("the moat = dataset + harness, not weights").
- **The business shape is "engine/API", not "consumer app" or even "academy SaaS".** Indian comparables monetize venues/coaching, not analysis subscriptions; Game Theory bundles highlights quasi-free; SwingVision — the best analog — took ~8 years to ~$2.75M revenue growing 12% YoY. That's a fine niche business and a poor venture story. The most credible GTM is selling the indexing capability per-hour *through* the players who look like competitors (PB Vision × PodPlay is the proven template) — VISIST/Machaxi have distribution and no rally-segmentation tech.
- **The commoditization clock is real but not expired.** Gemini-class models already do coarse highlights wrapper-cheap; the 2025–26 temporal-grounding literature (and the F3Set racket-sport benchmark) confirms precise boundaries remain hard for VLMs — which is exactly your head-first bet. I'd fund that bet, but **run the cheapest moat test first: a Gemini-3-Flash wrapper scored against your n=6 LOVO corpus with the harness you already have.** If a wrapper lands within a few F1 points of the learned 0.583, the owned model is premature and distribution is the whole game.
- **Sequencing implication:** the still-undone C13 discovery interviews (now with two added questions — "do you have multi-court footage nobody watches?" and "would you pay per-match to index it?") + the wrapper baseline + one paid pilot at any price are each cheaper than the async-job slice, and any of them could redirect months of engineering. The TT finding plus Stupa's federation traction also make **table tennis a genuinely underrated second beachhead** — less celebrity-locked than Bangalore badminton.

## Where this leaves you

1. **Fix master first** — the chip is ready (`task_2b7a19d4`); it includes the smoke-test guard so this class of bug can't ship green again. A minimal CI job is the natural follow-up.
2. **One doc-sync PR** would close inconsistencies #1–#8 (back-propagate MIT/BSD + Gemma-AMBER, fix the M0.3 pointer to `distill_local.py`, re-scope C3's mitigation honestly, link the plan/NEXT_STEPS from CLAUDE.md and the docs index, merge this branch).

All three threads are done. Here's where things stand.

## 1. Auditors — all 8 completed (Max-20x refresh worked)

The resume picked up the cached prefix and ran the five rate-limited auditors live (40 agents total). Net new findings beyond the first batch, all adversarially verified:

**One new critical, and it's a guardrail violation** — in the collector, not the indexer. `ingest.py` defaults `--license MIT`, and the ShuttleSet *annotation* license gets stamped onto the *YouTube broadcast video* it annotates. The committed export ships **24 videos / 1915 segments as `is_commercial=true, license_type=MIT`**, including a YONEX Thailand Open broadcast. The "commercially-clean training data" property the whole owned-model thesis rests on is currently certified on unsound grounds.

**Verified high-severity correctness/integrity bugs** (these are the ones that silently corrupt results or the corpus):
- **Detector artifacts keyed by file *basename*, not video_id** → two `match.mp4` files reuse stale frames → WASB emits one video's trajectory as another's, persisted as training data. The one place in the system not keyed by MD5.
- **Re-ingest is destroy-before-confirm** — `add_video` cascade-deletes prior good segments *before* the new run; a failed/empty re-run leaves zero.
- **Nested config silently drops unknown keys** — the entire `indexing.wasb` block (weights, conda env, velocity threshold) is unconfigurable via config.json; hardcoded defaults always win. CODE_MAP even documents these as if they were tunable.
- **`/api/process` arbitrary file-read + `/api/compile` path-traversal write**; **`run_regression` "CI gate" silently passes** with no baseline; **`match_intervals` at iou=0 scores garbage as 1.0**; **`rally_seq_proto` AUC has no tie handling** (and dead-time rows guarantee ties).
- **Collector:** silent destructive replace of golden labels; **validate-delivery PASSES on a zero-rally CVAT export**; the `int(float())` landmine guard exists but isn't wired into `import-local`.

The verifiers were honest in both directions — they **downgraded two "high" findings to not-real** (the Result-contract gap and DB exception-swallowing are documented, deliberate, incremental; one claim — "no busy_timeout" — was factually wrong since sqlite3 defaults to 5s). And they confirmed the genuine strengths: the registry/ABC seams, the DetectorRunner abstraction, the WASB crash-recovery cache, the leakage-free LOVO, and the frame-true CVAT conversion are all real, good engineering.

PR-1 from my earlier draft (the compiler SyntaxError) already landed while we worked — **#63 merged, master unbroken, and CI now exists.**

## 2. Spoof-check — the quality iterations are real

I didn't trust the docs; I re-ran the evals on this machine from the raw artifacts (pure numpy/scipy, no GPU). All six videos, six human label CSVs, and six trajectories exist, and trajectory row-counts match the docs exactly. Both headline numbers reproduced:

- **Learned prototype LOVO: 0.583** (per-video AUC 0.877/0.851/0.916/0.832/0.730/0.902 vs documented 0.879/0.853/0.915/0.833/0.726/0.902)
- **Heuristic LOVO: 0.480 ± 0.242**, per-fold Adarsh 0.751 / Kushagra 0.157 / doubles 0.737 / gBaaddy 0.309 / TestLarge 0.267 / Mahadevpura 0.657 — exact match
- **Contrast metric, recomputed independently from raw CSVs:** 3.7/1.4/3.7/1.9/1.4/2.2× vs documented 3.9/1.4/3.6/1.9/1.4/2.2×

Opus 4.8 did **not** spoof you here. One trivial nit: the gBaaddy CSV has 48 rallies, the doc says 47. The only thing I can't independently regenerate is the WASB trajectories themselves (GPU), but their sizes, frame counts, and visibility patterns are all physically sensible. The eng-eval auditor did add a fair methodological caveat: at n=6, mean±stdev can't statistically distinguish the +0.10 learned-vs-heuristic gap from noise — the *per-video* paired wins on the hard footage are the real signal, and the M0.4 harness should compute a paired sign/Wilcoxon test rather than lean on the mean.

440	    def export_eval_set(self, args):
441	        """Export curated annotations as indexer-ready eval/training sets.
442	
443	        Emits, per qualifying video, a `<out_dir>/<sport>/<video_id>.csv` in the
444	        indexer's `start,end` ground-truth format (decimal seconds), plus a single
445	        `<out_dir>/manifest.json` that pairs each CSV with its video file. The
446	        manifest is the contract the downstream eval/training driver reads: the
447	        indexer keys videos by *file MD5*, not by our `video_id`, so it must run
448	        against the exact `local_path`/`video_url` recorded here.
449	
450	        By default only CURATED + commercially-safe videos are exported, mirroring
451	        the license gate already enforced elsewhere in the toolchain.
452	        """

    def parse(self, filepath: str, **kwargs) -> Tuple[VideoMetadata, List[BadmintonRally]]:
        """
        Parses a CoachAI/ShuttleSet CSV format.

        Expected CSV Columns (any subset or mapped names):
            - set: Set number (1, 2, 3)
            - rally: Rally number
            - ball_round: Shot number within the rally (1, 2, 3...)
            - time: Hitting time of the shot (in seconds)
            - type: Stroke type (e.g., smash, lob, net...)
            - score_a / score_b: Current scores
        """
        if not os.path.exists(filepath):
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"File not found: {filepath}")

        # Extract video details from kwargs or name
        match_name = kwargs.get("match_name") or os.path.basename(filepath).replace(".csv", "")

git status --short
git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
fix(licensing): gate commercial use on the VIDEO license, not the annotation license

The ShuttleSet/CoachAI annotation license (MIT) was being stamped onto third-party
broadcast video, so `is_commercial` certified broadcast footage as commercially clean —
the manifest exported 23 YouTube-sourced videos as MIT/commercial, violating the
"training data must be commercial-clean" guardrail.

- VideoMetadata gains `annotation_license` (provenance only; never gates commercial use);
  `license_type` is now explicitly the VIDEO's rights.
- CoachAI parser + `ingest.py`: `--license` is an alias for `--annotation-license`
  (default MIT); the new `--video-license` defaults to Unknown, so broadcast footage is
  non-commercial unless rights are actually asserted. ingest warns when not commercial.
- DB: `annotation_license` column + idempotent migration; read mappers DRYed into
  `_row_to_video`.
- New `curate reclassify-licenses [--apply]` corrects existing conflated rows (dry-run
  found 23: every ShuttleSet broadcast row → annotation_license=MIT, video=Unknown,
  is_commercial=False). The committed corpus DB is intentionally left for the owner to
  reclassify + re-export deliberately.
- Tests: licensing-gate regression suite; updated two parser tests that asserted the old
  conflated behavior. Adds collector CI (pytest) — previously none existed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git log --oneline -1

- **Collector CI** added (pytest) — the repo previously had none.

9	- Swap in (or A/B test) a Linux-native implementation later with zero changes to
10	  the hybrid segmenters or the model-agnostic windowing brain.
11	- Provide a single place to evolve the healthcheck / error contract and thread
12	  detector readiness into per-video reports.
13	
14	Contract (deliberately matches what the concrete runners + hybrids + tests already did):
15	- run_predict(video_win_path: str, output_win_dir: str) -> Optional[str]
16	  Run detector, return the Windows-side path to the produced trajectory CSV

fix(detectors): namespace WSL/cache/output artifacts by video_id, not basename

WASB/TrackNet staged the video, extracted frames, the resumable cache, and the output
CSV under the file BASENAME. Two different videos sharing a filename (VID_0001.mp4,
match.mp4 — common phone names) would reuse each other's staged frames: wasb_infer's
extract_frames skips re-extraction when enough PNGs exist and manifest_compatible matched
on path+count, so the GPU pass was skipped and the wrong video's trajectory was emitted
and persisted as candidate_segments — silent training-data poisoning. The detector layer
was the one place not keyed by MD5.

- run_predict gains an optional video_id; staged video / frames_dir / cache / output CSV
  are namespaced as "<stem>__<md5[:12]>" so same-filename + different-bytes never collide.
- Both hybrid callers pass video_id (already in scope).
- Back-compat preserved (video_id omitted -> stem, as before).
- Tests: same-basename/different-id isolation + back-compat + TrackNet staged naming.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

## Why
Deep-audit **high** finding (verified): WASB/TrackNet keyed all WSL artifacts by file **basename**. Two videos sharing a filename (`VID_0001.mp4`, `match.mp4`) reuse each other's staged frames — `wasb_infer.extract_frames` skips re-extraction when enough PNGs exist and `manifest_compatible` matched on path+count, so the GPU pass was skipped and **the wrong video's trajectory was emitted and persisted as `candidate_segments`** (silent training-data poisoning). - Both hybrid callers (`wasb_hybrid`, `tracknet_hybrid`) pass `video_id` (already in scope).
- Back-compat: `video_id` omitted → falls back to the bare stem (existing behavior; existing tests unchanged).

- `tests/test_detector_keying.py`: same-basename/different-`video_id` produce distinct CSVs + distinct frame dirs; back-compat without id; TrackNet staged-output namespacing.
- Full suite: **259 passed**.

fix(ingest): re-ingest no longer destroys prior good segments (destroy-after-confirm)

add_video used INSERT OR REPLACE; with foreign_keys ON, REPLACE cascade-deleted a video's
play/candidate segments on ANY status update. It ran before the segmenter ('processed')
and on the failed-validation path, so a transient ffprobe hiccup, a tightened threshold,
or a re-POST whose new run produced nothing permanently destroyed prior results (incl.
human_label rows in candidate_segments).

- add_video is now an UPSERT (ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE) — status updates never touch children.
- New segment_watermarks() + prune_segments(): capture pre-run max ids, then on a non-empty
  run drop the OLD rows (keep new), and on an empty/failed run drop the NEW partial rows
  (keep old). main.py API + CLI paths use _finalize_reingest() to commit this.
- Tests: upsert preserves segments; prune keep-new/keep-old; empty-run keeps prior data.

command: gh pr create --repo avidullu/badminton-highlight-indexer --base master --head fix/reingest-destroy-after-confirm --title "Re-ingest: stop destroying prior good segments (destroy-after-confirm)" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Why
Deep-audit **high** finding (verified): `add_video` used `INSERT OR REPLACE`; with `foreign_keys` ON, REPLACE deletes the conflicting `videos` row and **cascade-deletes its play/candidate segments**. It ran *before* the segmenter (marking `processed`) and on the failed-validation path, so a transient ffprobe hiccup, a tightened validation threshold, or re-POSTing a video whose new run produced nothing **permanently destroyed prior results** — including `human_label`/`notes` rows in `candidate_segments` (the training corpus).

## What changed
- `add_video` is now an **UPSERT** (`ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE`) — a status update mutates the row in place and never cascades into children.
- **Destroy-after-confirm** for (re)segmentation: `segment_watermarks()` captures the pre-run max ids; after the run, `prune_segments()` keeps the NEW rows and drops the OLD on a non-empty result, or drops the NEW partial rows and keeps the OLD on an empty/failed run. Both the API and CLI paths use `_finalize_reingest()`.

## Tests
- `tests/test_reingest_safety.py`: upsert preserves segments; prune keep-new/keep-old; empty-run keeps prior data; zero watermarks.
- Full suite: **263 passed**; `import backend.main` OK.

import csv as _csv

from src.parsers.cvat.rally_cvat import (

    write_review_csv,
)
from src.cli.curate import SportsDataCLI


# --- helpers ---------------------------------------------------------------

def _img_box(frame, attrs):
    rows = "".join(f'<attribute name="{k}">{v}</attribute>' for k, v in attrs.items())
    return (f'<image id="{frame}" name="frame_{frame:06d}" width="1920" height="1080">'
            f'<box label="rally" xtl="1" ytl="1" xbr="2" ybr="2">{rows}</box></image>')


def _write_cvat(path, images, step=30, stop_frame=1000):
    body = "".join(images)
    xml = (
        '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?><annotations><version>1.1</version>'
        f'<meta><job><stop_frame>{stop_frame}</stop_frame>'
        f'<frame_filter>step={step}</frame_filter></job></meta>'
        f'{body}</annotations>'
    )
    path.write_text(xml, encoding="utf-8")
    return str(path)


def _rec(rn, start, end, shots=5, reason="winner", fmin=None, fmax=None, n=3, outcome=None):
    return RallyRecord(
        rally_number=rn, start_time=start, end_time=end, shots_count=shots,

command: git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
fix(cvat): fail the delivery gate on empty/corrupt/zipped CVAT instead of passing

The --input CVAT path had no emptiness guard (unlike --csv), so a delivery that parsed to
ZERO rallies (wrong job exported, or a renamed rally_number attribute -> all boxes skipped)
printed "GATE: PASS". Corrupt XML raised an uncaught ParseError traceback (ParseError
subclasses SyntaxError, not the caught ValueError), breaking the CI exit-code contract. The
standard CVAT delivery artifact — a .zip containing annotations.xml — was unsupported.

- parse_cvat_boxes accepts a .zip (reads annotations.xml) and converts ParseError to a
  ValueError, so callers' existing (FileNotFoundError, ValueError) handling yields a clean
  non-zero exit instead of a traceback.
- convert-cvat and validate-delivery now reject a zero-rally parse (exit 1 / GATE: BLOCKED).
- Tests: empty -> 0 records + gate BLOCKED; corrupt -> ValueError; zip -> parsed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

48	def match_intervals(preds: List[Interval], gts: List[Interval],
49	                    iou_threshold: float = 0.5) -> MatchResult:
50	    """Greedy one-to-one matching of predictions to ground truth by descending IoU.
51	
52	    Every candidate (pred, gt) pair with IoU >= threshold is considered; pairs
53	    are claimed highest-IoU first, and each prediction/GT can be used once. This
54	    keeps a single prediction from being credited for two ground-truth rallies
55	    (and vice versa).
56	    """
57	    candidates = []
58	    for pi, p in enumerate(preds):
59	        for gi, g in enumerate(gts):
60	            iou = interval_iou(p, g)
61	            if iou >= iou_threshold:
62	                candidates.append((iou, pi, gi))
63	    # Highest IoU first; ties broken by indices for determinism.
64	    candidates.sort(key=lambda c: (-c[0], c[1], c[2]))
65	
66	    used_pred, used_gt = set(), set()
67	    matches: List[Match] = []
68	    for iou, pi, gi in candidates:
69	        if pi in used_pred or gi in used_gt:
70	            continue
71	        used_pred.add(pi)
72	        used_gt.add(gi)
73	        matches.append(Match(pred_index=pi, gt_index=gi, iou=iou))
74	
75	    unmatched_pred = [i for i in range(len(preds)) if i not in used_pred]
76	    unmatched_gt = [i for i in range(len(gts)) if i not in used_gt]
77	    return MatchResult(matches=matches,
78	                       unmatched_pred_indices=unmatched_pred,
79	                       unmatched_gt_indices=unmatched_gt)

7	    ground truth  ← AnnotationProvider (file / vendor / oracle)  [backend.annotations]
8	    predictions   ← the production pipeline's stored DB rows     [backend.eval.harness]
9	    comparison    ← interval matching + P/R/F1                   [backend.eval.metrics]
10	    baseline      ← a per-video snapshot of "known good" numbers [this module]
11	
12	A "regression" is a precision/recall drop beyond `tolerance` versus the snapshotted
13	baseline. Tiers map to annotation providers: e.g. tier "file" → FileProvider (CI),
14	later tier "vendor" → HumanVendorProvider (authoritative), tier "auto" → an
15	independent-lineage oracle (fast smoke alarm). See docs/GOLDEN_SET_IMPLEMENTATION.md.

66

69	    """Snapshot a video/stage's current numbers as the new 'known good' baseline.

72	    baselines don't raise false regressions. Stored as plain JSON for easy diffing.
73	    """
74	    baselines = load_baselines(path)
75	    baselines[_baseline_key(video_id, stage)] = {
76	        "video_id": video_id, "stage": stage,
77	        "precision": precision, "recall": recall, "f1": f1,
78	    }
79	    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path) or ".", exist_ok=True)
80	    with open(path, "w") as f:
81	        json.dump(baselines, f, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
82	    logger.info("Saved baseline for %s (precision=%.3f recall=%.3f)", _baseline_key(video_id, stage), precision, recall)

### 631. assistant (2026-07-02T06:11:32.927Z)

[external_agent_tool_result]
1	"""CLI: regression-test the production tool against golden-set ground truth.
2	
3	Obtains ground truth from an annotation provider (a tier), scores the video's
4	stored predictions, and compares to a snapshotted baseline. Exit code 1 on a
5	detected regression so it can gate CI. See docs/GOLDEN_SET_IMPLEMENTATION.md.
6	
7	Examples
8	--------
9	Snapshot the current numbers as the baseline (first run / after a real improvement):
10	    python run_regression.py --video-id <md5> --tier file --annotations rallies.csv --update-baseline
11	
12	Check for a regression (exit 1 if precision/recall dropped beyond tolerance):
13	    python run_regression.py --video-id <md5> --tier file --annotations rallies.csv
14	"""
15	import os
16	import sys
17	import json
18	import argparse
19	import logging
20	
21	from backend.infrastructure.database import Database
22	from backend.config import load_config
23	from backend.annotations import annotation_registry
24	from backend.eval import regression
25	
26	
27	def _default_db_path() -> str:
28	    cfg = load_config()
29	    return os.path.join(cfg.output.output_dir, cfg.output.db_name)
30	
31	
32	def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
33	    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Regression-test the tool vs golden-set ground truth.")
34	    p.add_argument("--video-id", required=True, help="Stored video_id (MD5) whose predictions to score.")
35	    p.add_argument("--tier", default="file",
36	                   help=f"Annotation provider tier. Available: {annotation_registry.list_available()}")
37	    p.add_argument("--annotations", help="video_ref for the provider (e.g. CSV path for the 'file' tier).")
38	    p.add_argument("--stage", choices=("candidates", "final"), default="final")
39	    p.add_argument("--detector", default=None, help="Restrict candidate scoring to one detector.")
40	    p.add_argument("--iou", type=float, default=0.5)
41	    p.add_argument("--tolerance", type=float, default=regression.DEFAULT_TOLERANCE)
42	    p.add_argument("--db", default=None)
43	    p.add_argument("--baseline", default=regression.DEFAULT_BASELINE_PATH, help="Baseline JSON path.")
44	    p.add_argument("--update-baseline", action="store_true",
45	                   help="Snapshot the current numbers as the new baseline instead of checking.")
46	    p.add_argument("--json", dest="json_out", default=None)
47	    return p
48	
49	
50	def main(argv=None) -> int:
51	    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
52	    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
53	
54	    db_path = args.db or _default_db_path()
55	    if not os.path.exists(db_path):
56	        print(f"ERROR: database not found at {db_path}. Run the pipeline first.", file=sys.stderr)
57	        return 2
58	    db = Database(db_path)
59	
60	    result = regression.regress_with_provider(
61	        db, video_id=args.video_id, video_ref=args.annotations, tier=args.tier,
62	        stage=args.stage, iou_threshold=args.iou, detector=args.detector,
63	        tolerance=args.tolerance, baseline_path=args.baseline,
64	    )
65	
66	    print(regression.format_result(result))
67	
68	    if args.update_baseline:
69	        regression.save_baseline(result.video_id, result.stage, result.precision,
70	                                 result.recall, result.f1, path=args.baseline)
71	        print(f"Baseline updated in {args.baseline}.")
72	
73	    if args.json_out:
74	        with open(args.json_out, "w") as f:
75	            json.dump(result.as_dict(), f, indent=2)
76	        print(f"JSON written to {args.json_out}")
77	
78	    # Non-zero exit on regression so CI can gate on it.
79	    return 1 if result.regressed else 0
80	
81	
82	if __name__ == "__main__":
83	    raise SystemExit(main())
84

command: git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
fix(eval): trustworthy regression gate + correct metric/AUC/feature footguns

Three eval-trustworthiness fixes that gate the owned-model decision:

1. metrics.match_intervals at iou_threshold=0.0 matched completely disjoint intervals
   (IoU 0.0 satisfied `iou >= 0`), fabricating perfect scores. Now requires real overlap.

2. rally_seq_proto.roc_auc had no tie handling (sequential ranks via argsort) — an
   all-tied classifier scored an order-dependent 0.25..0.75 instead of 0.5, and dead-time
   frames are all-zero feature rows (guaranteed ties). Now uses midranks (scipy rankdata).
   Also: speed features are now per-SECOND (* fps) instead of per-frame, so the same
   physical speed no longer reads ~2x smaller at 59.94 vs 30 fps (a real cross-footage
   confound on a mixed-fps corpus); speed/crossings are not computed across occlusion gaps.

3. run_regression was a CI gate in name only: the baseline lived under gitignored output/
   and a missing baseline silently passed (exit 0). Now the default baseline path is the
   tracked eval_baselines/; a missing baseline exits 3 (gate cannot verify) unless
   --update-baseline/--allow-missing-baseline; and the baseline records iou/detector/GT-hash
   so a run at a different IoU or against changed labels is flagged as incommensurable.

Re-ran the n=6 LOVO after the corrections: learned mean held-out F1 0.583 -> 0.626 (the
fps-normalization helped cross-footage transfer; per-video AUC unchanged at 0.83-0.92,
confirming it was never tie-inflated). Heuristic LOVO (0.480, scored at IoU 0.5) is
unaffected. The learned-beats-heuristic conclusion holds and widens.

Tests: iou=0 no longer matches disjoint; AUC midrank ties -> 0.5; missing-baseline exit 3;
allow-missing exit 0; IoU/label mismatch flagged incommensurable.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

command: git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
fix(reliability): bound WSL/provider timeouts, SQLite WAL+busy_timeout, chunk-step guard, CORS

A batch of medium-severity hardening from the audit:
- WSL detector timeout_sec default 0 (= hang forever) -> 1800s in both runners + the typed
  config + config.json (0 still means "no timeout" for power users).
- Gemini PROCESSING poll was unbounded; add a 20-min deadline so a stuck remote file can't
  wedge the worker thread / request indefinitely.
- SQLite: open with WAL + busy_timeout=30s (and connect timeout) so concurrent writers wait
  rather than hit an immediate, swallowed "database is locked" once the async job model lands.
- IndexingConfig rejects chunk_overlap >= chunk_duration at load time (a non-positive step
  made the chunk loop spin forever, growing memory before any GPU work).
- CORS: allow_credentials=False (wildcard origin + credentials is browser-rejected and an
  unsafe default to carry into the auth/tenancy work; the tool uses no cookies).

Deferred with intent (noted for follow-up): shlex-quoting WSL config values would break the
`~` home-expansion those paths rely on; lazy torch/cv2 imports and an app-factory/lifespan
refactor belong with the owner-gated async-job slice; WSL temp/frame/cache GC needs a
retention-policy decision.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [master]
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  # Fast guard against the 7fbbeb0 class of breakage: a SyntaxError or
  # module-level import error shipping while the suite stays green.
  # Deliberately does NOT install cv2/torch/numpy — the smoke tests must hold
  # on machines without the GPU stack (test_import_smoke stubs what's absent).
  import-smoke:
    name: Syntax sweep + import smoke (no GPU stack)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"
      - name: Install minimal deps
        run: python -m pip install pytest fastapi uvicorn pydantic python-dotenv google-genai
      - name: Run import smoke tests
        run: python -m pytest tests/test_import_smoke.py -v

  full-suite:
    name: Full test suite (offline, mocked)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"
          cache: pip
      - name: System libs for opencv-python
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y libgl1 libglib2.0-0t64 || sudo apt-get install -y libgl1 libglib2.0-0
      - name: Install CPU-only torch (no CUDA wheels on a CPU runner)
        run: python -m pip install torch torchvision --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu
      - name: Install requirements
        run: python -m pip install -r requirements.txt pytest
      # obsreport (private, soft dep) is absent here: reporting tests skip via
      # pytest.importorskip — run_all_tests.py prints which.
      - name: Run full suite
        run: python run_all_tests.py

Stage 1 runs **torchvision person detection** (Faster R-CNN, BSD-licensed) with **ByteTrack** tracking (supervision, MIT-licensed) to cheaply filter the video down to a small set of high-motion candidate windows. Stage 2 hands each candidate (with a small padding) to the AI provider for high-precision semantic boundaries and shot counts. Massively cheaper than running the LLM on the full video. *(The registry key remains `yolo_hybrid` for back-compat; the AGPL-licensed YOLOv8 was replaced with permissive components — see [docs/archives/MONETIZATION_AUDIT.md](docs/archives/MONETIZATION_AUDIT.md) and ADR-005.)*
21	    *   `gemini` — sends the entire video (or a `chunk_duration` slice) to Google Gemini directly. Highest precision per call, highest cost.
22	    *   `motion` — zero-dependency OpenCV pixel-difference heuristic. No API key required. Useful as a baseline or for offline/air-gapped use.
[/external_agent_tool_result]

173	### Q3: How do I add a new custom validator to the pipeline?
174	1. Create a new python file in `backend/validators/` (e.g. `my_check.py`).
175	2. Subclass `VideoValidator` and implement `validate(self, video_path, config, context)`.
176	3. Register your class inside `backend/validators/__init__.py` using `registry.register(MyCheckValidator())`.
177	It's that simple! The app will automatically run it, display it in the CLI diagnostics summary, and render it in the frontend checklist.

### 976. assistant (2026-07-02T06:11:32.945Z)

Good news on both fronts — and the check I just ran makes this concrete. Your pending uncommitted DB change turns out to be **schema-only** (the new empty pickleball/tabletennis tables plus the `annotation_license` column migration — partly a side effect of my PR-A preview opening the DB). Row content is byte-for-byte identical to the committed version: same 25 videos, same 1917 rallies, same licenses. So there's nothing mysterious to protect there.

## What `reclassify-licenses --apply` actually does

It updates **metadata on exactly 23 rows** in the `videos` table — the `shuttleset_*` entries (all have a YouTube `video_url` + `license_type=MIT`). For each: `MIT` moves to the new `annotation_license` column (provenance), `license_type` becomes `Unknown`, `is_commercial` flips 1→0.

What it does **not** do:

- **No annotations deleted** — all 1,917 ShuttleSet rallies stay in the DB, fully queryable.
- **No files touched** — videos on disk, trajectories, labels, the indexer DB: all untouched.
- **Your own entries untouched** — `my_custom_local_match` (Proprietary) and anything without a remote URL are skipped by design. And notably, your six golden matches (Adarsh, Kushagra, etc.) **aren't in the collector DB at all yet** — their import is the pending M0.1 milestone — so they can't be affected.

The follow-up `curate export` is where the visible change happens: the default (curated + commercial-only) manifest shrinks to essentially just the mock entry, because the 23 ShuttleSet broadcasts no longer qualify as commercial training data. If you want ShuttleSet for **eval-only** continuity, `curate export --include-staging --include-noncommercial --out-dir data/eval_export_research` gives you a clearly-labeled research manifest — using a public dataset's annotations to *measure* is standard practice; the guardrail only forbids them in *training* views.

## Do the quality signals need regenerating? **No.**

The headline numbers — learned LOVO **0.626** vs heuristic **0.480**, the per-video AUCs, the contrast metric, the WASB→TT/pickleball transfer results — are computed entirely from `output/human_lovo_manifest.json` + your own videos' labels in `Annotation Setup/Collect/Golden Labelled/` + the trajectories now in `Annotation Setup/Collect/Trajectories/`. That path never goes through the collector DB or its export, and I re-verified 0.626 from the durable locations today. The only thing reclassification changes going forward is the **composition of future corpus-aggregate runs** over the collector export (`run_phase3_eval.py`) — old ShuttleSet-era numbers remain valid as historical records, but new aggregate runs over the commercial export won't include those 23 videos unless you explicitly opt in.

## One ownership clarification (the important nuance)

You own your six recorded matches — and those are exactly the videos your quality signals rest on, which is why nothing needs regenerating. But the 23 affected rows are **ShuttleSet broadcast footage** (YONEX Thailand Open etc.) — CoachAI's MIT license covers their *annotation CSVs*, not the BWF/broadcaster's *video*, and downloading it doesn't confer footage rights. That's precisely the conflation the fix targets. Your "I can regenerate if needed" instinct is the right long-term answer in a different sense: the plan's own thesis is that the moat is your **owned, consented corpus** — importing your golden matches into the collector as `Proprietary` (M0.1) replaces ShuttleSet's role with data you genuinely own.

## Suggested sequence when you run it

```
cd sports-data-collector
copy data\sports_metadata.db data\sports_metadata.backup.db   # cheap insurance
python -m src.cli.curate reclassify-licenses                  # dry-run, eyeball the 23
python -m src.cli.curate reclassify-licenses --apply
python -m src.cli.curate export                               # regenerate the commercial manifest
git add data\sports_metadata.db data\eval_export && git commit
```

(The schema-only pending diff folds naturally into that same commit.) Optional extras while you're in there: drop the mock `my_custom_local_match` from the corpus DB (it's demo data the audit flagged), and keep the backup copy out of git. Happy to run the whole sequence for you now if you'd like — it's reversible via the backup either way.

### 1024. assistant (2026-07-02T06:11:32.948Z)

## 1. The field plan — yes, bake the camera idea in. It's the strongest version of the validation.

Recruiting a socially-fluent interviewer is exactly right (founder-led discovery fails more on awkwardness than on questions). The camera addition turns "would you hypothetically pay?" into "here is *your* footage, indexed" — and it simultaneously manufactures the one asset we just made scarce: after the ShuttleSet reclassification, your commercial training corpus is owned-data-only, and **paid recordings at academies = consented, owned, multi-court footage in the exact target distribution**. Every recorded match is both a demo and an n+1 for LOVO. Three design constraints to bake in:

1. **Consent at capture, not after.** A one-page footage release per academy + per-player consent, and **adults-only sessions for anything entering the training pool** (the minors-exclusion guardrail is non-negotiable). These recordings should become the first real entries in the M0.1 consent ledger — don't let the demo punch a hole in the corpus we just cleaned.
2. **Don't gate the demo on the owned model — it isn't at 0.8 yet.** Honest numbers: the learned prototype's LOVO mean is 0.626 — roughly 0.70–0.74 on clean singles, 0.51–0.53 on multi-court. The >0.8 customer-visible bar today is reachable two ways, both legitimate: **(a) the paid Gemini path** (inference/serving is explicitly allowed by your guardrails; ~$0.05–0.30/video) — e.g. `gemini_refine` over WASB candidates; or **(b) auto-generate + 15 minutes of human polish in rally-annotator**, which doubles as golden labels. My recommendation: run **both** the owned prototype and the Gemini path on every recorded video, demo whichever wins — because that comparison *is* the Gemini-wrapper-baseline experiment from NEXT_STEPS item 3. One field trip, three deliverables: demand signal, consented corpus, moat test.
3. **Sequence: interviews first, cameras second.** The two added questions ("do you have multi-court footage nobody watches?" / "would you pay per-match to index it?") identify which academies *already record* — and indexing their **existing** footage is an even stronger demo than new recordings, since it tests the BYO-footage wedge directly. Pilot cameras at the 2–3 warmest academies from round one. Hand your interviewer `VIDEO_RECORDING_GUIDELINES.md` as the capture spec; the observability report will auto-flag bad capture (nice dogfood).

I'll draft the interview one-pager + structured answer sheet + a consent-release template whenever you want them.

## 2. The repo question — your instinct is right; the *timing* is where I'll push back

I ran this through an adversarial panel (separate-repo advocate, monorepo advocate, ML-infra practitioner, cross-examiner — all grounded in the actual code), and the verdict is one I largely agree with:

**Draw the boundary you want NOW — at the artifact contract. Split the repo at Gen-2, as a pre-committed, trigger-based event — not today.**

The isolation you're after ("iterate on model and processing independently") is real and correct, but the load-bearing boundary in ML systems is **"serving loads only a versioned artifact (weights + featurizer + manifest), never training code"** — not a repo wall. The indexer already consumes WASB exactly this way. Three verified facts argue against a separate repo *today*:

- **The WASB analogy breaks at the seam location.** WASB's contract sits at the video boundary (video in → trajectory CSV out); Gemini's at video → segments. But the Gen-0 TAL head consumes **features the indexer itself computes** from the trajectory — `rally_seq_proto` imports the trajectory parser, the golden-label loader (shared with seven eval modules), the metrics spine, and the classifier. The seam is *mid-pipeline*. And since the indexer is an app, not a pip-installable package, a separate repo today can only get that code by **copying it** — which is this project's one empirically observed failure mode, twice this week (the `start,end` vs `start_time,end_time` loader fork; the duplicated TUNED constants). The fps-normalization bug I just fixed is precisely the train/serve-skew class a copied featurizer breeds.
- **Your collector precedent actually argues contract-first, not split-first.** The header fork happened *across exactly that boundary* — and the cross-examiner verified the obsreport precedent has never truly been exercised: its requirements pin is a commented-out line, the repo's never published, CI skips it. It survives because its absence is harmless. A featurizer's absence or drift never is.
- **Gen-0 has no forcing function; Gen-2 genuinely does.** The head trains in minutes at ~4.5GB on your 2070S with MIT pip-able deps. ms-swift + Qwen3-VL + rented cloud GPUs is an alien dependency tree you should *never* want inside the product repo — that's the natural split moment, and by then the contract will be proven, making extraction a file move instead of a guess.

**So the concrete design I'd greenlight for M0.4/M0.1** (this honors your isolation preference as a scheduled commitment, per your own "envision now, build later" principle):

1. **`training/` as a top-level tree** (sibling of `backend/`), with an *executable* wall: its own `requirements-train.txt`, a third CI lane, and the import-smoke test extended to assert `import backend.main` loads no training module. Isolation enforced by CI, not etiquette.
2. **Promote the featurizer** out of `rally_seq_proto` into `backend/features/rally_seq.py` (pure numpy, versioned schema constant) — imported by *both* the training harness and the future TAL segmenter. Train == serve by construction.
3. **Artifact bundle from day one:** weights gitignored + private GitHub Releases (Gen-0 weights are kilobytes); a *committed* manifest carrying feature-schema version, normalization params, calibration/post-processing, corpus ref + GT-hash, and a consent/license attestation — including WASB C3 status, so the gate mechanically refuses commercial ship while C3 is open. The serving runner is just another registered segmenter that loads the artifact and hard-fails on schema mismatch.
4. **The ship-gate stays product-side** (extend the regression gate we just hardened) — the trainer must never grade itself.
5. **Pre-commit the split in the plan**: destination repo named now (e.g. `sports-temporal-models`, slotting into your rename), trigger = *Gen-2/cloud training arrives OR a second artifact consumer appears, AND the harness's only data input is the collector's M0.1 export*.

One thing the panel flagged that must come **first**, before any ActionFormer epoch: **freeze the golden-label/corpus contract.** The indexer today carries *two incompatible GT loaders* against a collector that exports a third-party's pick of the two formats — and every quantity the ship-gate depends on (GT-hash, LOVO numbers, the future consent fingerprint) flows through that boundary. One versioned loader + the M0.1 JSONL schema + a cross-repo round-trip test. Related: the n=6 corpus's durable home is currently a loose `Annotation Setup\` folder — *neither* repo — so M0.1's first deliverable should be ingesting it into the collector, hash-addressed.

If you ratify this, my opening sequence for M0.4+M0.1 would be: **ADR (recording this decision + the split trigger) → GT-loader consolidation + round-trip test → featurizer promotion + import wall → golden-corpus ingestion into the collector → then the Gen-0 harness itself**, with the Gemini-wrapper baseline run alongside. Say the word and I'll start with the ADR.

**Date:** 2026-05-25
**Status:** Accepted

### Context

The pipeline uses an AI multimodal provider (Gemini) for *semantic* rally segmentation.
We need **precise frame-level detection of the moving shuttlecock** (and, generically,
balls for other sports) to produce higher-quality candidate rallies and a fine-tuning
signal.

We evaluated whether a commercially available model/API could do this. Findings:

## ADR-008: Owned-model topology — artifact boundary now, repo split at Gen-2

**Date:** 2026-06-10
**Status:** Accepted (owner-ratified after an adversarial design panel)

### Context

M0.4 (Gen-0 TAL train→eval→ship-gate harness, productionizing `backend/eval/rally_seq_proto.py`
over ActionFormer/ASFormer) and M0.1 (corpus spine + event-index contract) are greenlit. The
question: should the model/training work live **in this repo**, or in a **separate repo** whose
output the indexer consumes as another segmenter (like WASB and Gemini)? The owner's instinct
was isolation ("iterate on model and processing independently"), citing the collector split as
precedent.

### Decision

**Draw the boundary at the ARTIFACT CONTRACT now; split the repo at Gen-2, as a pre-committed,
trigger-based event — not today.**

1. **Training lives in this repo as a top-level `training/` tree** (sibling of `backend/`),
   isolated *executably*, not socially: its own `training/requirements-train.txt` (heavy/
   training-only deps never enter `requirements.txt`), and the import-smoke suite asserts
   `import backend.main` loads **no `training.*` module**.
2. **The featurizer is single-source-of-truth**: promoted out of `rally_seq_proto` into
   `backend/features/rally_seq.py` (pure numpy/scipy, versioned schema constant), imported by
   BOTH the training harness and the future TAL serving segmenter. Train == serve by
   construction — the fps-normalization bug (fixed 2026-06-10) is the skew class this kills.
3. **Serving consumes only a versioned ARTIFACT BUNDLE** (weights gitignored / private GitHub
   Releases + a manifest carrying: feature-schema version, normalization, calibration/
   post-processing, training-corpus ref + GT hash, consent + license attestation incl. the
   WASB C3 checkpoint status). The loader/gate hard-fails on schema mismatch — the
   `regression.py` incommensurability-guard pattern.
4. **The ship-gate is owned by the product side** (extends `backend/eval/regression.py` +
   `metrics.match_intervals`): the trainer runs it as pre-flight but never grades itself.
   The gate refuses commercial ship while C3 is unresolved, regardless of F1.
5. **Pre-committed split trigger** — extract `training/` into a separate repo (working name
   `sports-temporal-models`, to be finalized with the pending repo rename) **when**:
   (a) Gen-2 arrives (ms-swift / Qwen3-VL / cloud-GPU training — an alien dependency tree), OR
   (b) a second consumer of the trained artifacts appears (e.g. the khelacharya layer),
   AND (c) the harness's only data input is the collector's M0.1 export. By then the artifact
   contract is proven and extraction is a file move across a known seam.

**Prerequisite frozen first: the golden-label/corpus contract.** One canonical GT loader (the
repo carried two incompatible ones: `annotations.load_annotations` `start,end` vs
`calibrate_wasb.load_golden_gts` `start_time,end_time`, the latter feeding 7 modules) + a
round-trip test against the collector's `curate export` format. Every ship-gate quantity
(gt_hash, LOVO numbers, the future consent fingerprint) flows through this boundary.

### Rationale (the decisive, code-verified facts)

- **The "just another runner like WASB/Gemini" analogy fails at the seam location.** WASB's
  contract sits at the video boundary (video → trajectory CSV); Gemini's at video → segments.
  The Gen-0 head consumes **features this repo computes** from the trajectory — the seam is
  mid-pipeline. Since the indexer is an app (not pip-installable), a separate repo today could
  share that code only by **copying** it — this project's one empirically observed failure
  mode (the GT-header fork; the duplicated TUNED constants).
- **The in-house separate-repo precedent is unproven for load-bearing deps**: the `obsreport`
  pin has never been live (commented in requirements.txt, repo unpublished, CI skips via
  importorskip). It works because its absence is a harmless no-op — a property a featurizer
  can never have.
- **Gen-0 has no environmental forcing function** (trains in minutes, ~4.5 GB, MIT pip-able
  deps, on the owner's WSL/2070S box); Gen-2 genuinely does. Splitting then is a scheduled
  event, not an overruled instinct.
- The prerequisite work for a clean split (featurizer promotion, loader consolidation,
  manifest) is **identical** to the in-repo design — doing it in place first makes the
  eventual extraction cheap and safe. This is "envision now, build later" applied to topology:
  **the split is driven by productionization needs, not code-isolation aesthetics** (owner's
  framing, ratified).

### Consequences

- `backend/` may never import `training.*` (CI-enforced). Training tests use **synthetic
  fixtures only** until the M0.1 consent ledger exists (no real trajectories/labels committed).
- Weights are never committed; artifact manifests are the reviewable/committable surface.
- The collector remains system-of-record for labels + consent; the indexer owns scoring and
  the ship/no-ship decision; manifests pin both by hash.
- Revisit triggers are explicit (above); if agent-driven development repeatedly breaches the
  import wall despite CI, that is evidence the social+test boundary failed and the split
  should happen early.

Panel artifacts: workflow `wf_471a9cdd-d1d` (3 grounded position papers + cross-examination),
2026-06-10.

1	"""Load hand-annotated ground-truth rally timestamps from CSV.
2	
3	Annotation file format (one file per video):
4	
5	    start,end
6	    00:01:12,00:01:39
7	    102.5,131.0
8	
9	- A header row `start,end` is optional (auto-detected and skipped).
10	- Each timestamp is either decimal seconds (`102.5`) or colon-separated
11	  `MM:SS` / `HH:MM:SS` (`00:01:12`). Both forms may be mixed in one file.
12	- Blank lines and `#` comment lines are ignored.
13	"""
14	
15	import csv
16	import logging
17	from typing import List, Tuple
18	
19	logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
20	
21	Interval = Tuple[float, float]
22	
23	
24	def parse_timestamp(value: str) -> float:
25	    """Parse a timestamp string to float seconds.
26	
27	    Accepts decimal seconds or colon-separated MM:SS / HH:MM:SS.
28	    Raises ValueError on anything unparseable so bad annotations fail loudly.
29	    """
30	    value = value.strip()
31	    if not value:
32	        raise ValueError("empty timestamp")
33	    if ":" in value:
34	        parts = value.split(":")
35	        if len(parts) > 3:
36	            raise ValueError(f"too many ':' segments in timestamp '{value}'")
37	        total = 0.0
38	        for part in parts:                 # most-significant first (H, M, S)
39	            total = total * 60 + float(part)
40	        return total
41	    return float(value)
42	
43	
44	def load_annotations(csv_path: str) -> List[Interval]:
45	    """Load and validate ground-truth rally intervals from a CSV file.
46	
47	    Returns intervals sorted by start time. Raises ValueError on malformed rows
48	    (bad timestamp, start >= end) so labeling mistakes surface immediately rather
49	    than silently skewing scores.
50	    """
51	    intervals: List[Interval] = []
52	    with open(csv_path, newline="") as f:
53	        reader = csv.reader(f)
54	        for lineno, row in enumerate(reader, start=1):
55	            if not row:
56	                continue
57	            first = row[0].strip()
58	            if not first or first.startswith("#"):
59	                continue
60	            # Skip an optional header row.
61	            if first.lower() in ("start", "start_time"):
62	                continue
63	            if len(row) < 2:
64	                raise ValueError(f"{csv_path}:{lineno}: expected 'start,end', got {row!r}")
65	            try:
66	                start = parse_timestamp(row[0])
67	                end = parse_timestamp(row[1])
68	            except ValueError as e:
69	                raise ValueError(f"{csv_path}:{lineno}: {e}") from e
70	            if start >= end:
71	                raise ValueError(f"{csv_path}:{lineno}: start ({start}) >= end ({end})")
72	            intervals.append((start, end))
73	
74	    intervals.sort(key=lambda iv: iv[0])
75	    logger.info("Loaded %d ground-truth rallies from %s", len(intervals), csv_path)
76	    return intervals
77	
78	
79	def write_scaffold(csv_path: str) -> None:
80	    """Write an empty annotation file with just the header, for hand-filling."""
81	    with open(csv_path, "w", newline="") as f:
82	        writer = csv.writer(f)
83	        writer.writerow(["start", "end"])

feat(eval): canonical GT loader — close the golden-CSV two-loader fork (ADR-008 prereq)

The repo carried two incompatible GT loaders: annotations.load_annotations (positional
start,end — the collector export format; could NOT read rally-annotator golden CSVs) and
calibrate_wasb.load_golden_gts (DictReader start_time/end_time; could NOT read collector
exports), the latter feeding 7 eval modules. A file in one convention fed to the other
loader produced zero/garbage intervals with no error.

- New backend/eval/gt_loader.py::load_gt_intervals — accepts BOTH conventions
  (header-mapped start|start_time / end|end_time, else positional), strict (raise with
  file:line) or lenient (skip + LOG count — no more silent shrinkage), warns on
  overlapping GT, sorts.
- load_annotations and load_golden_gts now delegate (strict / lenient respectively);
  signatures and consumers unchanged.

1	"""Import/syntax smoke tests for the backend package.
2	
3	Guards against a SyntaxError (or module-level import error) shipping while the
4	suite stays green: most of the suite imports individual backend modules, so a
5	broken file that nothing imports (e.g. the stitcher compiler, which only
6	backend.main pulls in) used to go unnoticed.
7	
8	Both tests are offline and dependency-light: the syntax sweep never imports
9	anything, and the backend.main import runs in a subprocess with any missing
10	heavy deps (cv2/torch/numpy) stubbed, so they also pass in environments
11	without the GPU stack.
12	"""
13	
14	import py_compile
15	import subprocess
16	import sys
17	from pathlib import Path
18	
19	REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
20	
21	
22	def test_backend_package_has_no_syntax_errors():
23	    """Every .py file under backend/ must byte-compile."""
24	    failures = []
25	    for path in sorted((REPO_ROOT / "backend").rglob("*.py")):
26	        try:
27	            py_compile.compile(str(path), doraise=True)
28	        except py_compile.PyCompileError as exc:
29	            failures.append(f"{path.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)}: {exc.msg}")
30	    assert not failures, "Syntax errors in backend/:\n" + "\n".join(failures)
31	
32	
33	def test_backend_main_imports():
34	    """backend.main (FastAPI app, /api/compile) must be importable.
35	
36	    Runs in a subprocess so stubbing missing heavy deps cannot leak into this
37	    pytest process; cwd=repo root puts the package on sys.path.
38	    """
39	    prelude = (
40	        "import importlib.util, sys\n"
41	        "from unittest import mock\n"
42	        "for name in ('cv2', 'torch', 'numpy'):\n"
43	        "    if importlib.util.find_spec(name) is None:\n"
44	        "        sys.modules[name] = mock.MagicMock()\n"
45	        "import backend.main\n"
46	    )
47	    result = subprocess.run(
48	        [sys.executable, "-c", prelude],
49	        cwd=str(REPO_ROOT),
50	        capture_output=True,
51	        text=True,
52	    )
53	    assert result.returncode == 0, (

129	        v = data[test]

76	
77	def probs_to_segments(probs: np.ndarray, times: np.ndarray, threshold: float,
78	                      merge_gap: float = 1.0, min_dur: float = 1.0, smooth: int = 7) -> List[Interval]:
79	    p = uniform_filter1d(probs, max(1, smooth), mode="nearest")
80	    on = p >= threshold
81	    runs: List[Interval] = []
82	    i, n = 0, len(on)
83	    while i < n:
84	        if on[i]:
85	            j = i
86	            while j + 1 < n and on[j + 1]:
87	                j += 1
88	            runs.append((float(times[i]), float(times[j])))
89	            i = j + 1
90	        else:
91	            i += 1
92	    merged: List[Interval] = []
93	    for s, e in runs:
94	        if merged and s - merged[-1][1] <= merge_gap:
95	            merged[-1] = (merged[-1][0], e)
96	        else:
97	            merged.append((s, e))
98	    return [(s, e) for s, e in merged if e - s >= min_dur]

15	def _write_traj(path, fps=10.0):
16	    """120s synthetic trajectory: shuttle oscillates fast across the net during 'rallies'
17	    (0-20s, 40-60s, 80-100s) and is mostly still/invisible in the dead time between."""
18	    rows = [("Frame", "Visibility", "X", "Y")]
19	    n = int(120 * fps)
20	    for f in range(n):
21	        t = f / fps
22	        in_rally = (t < 20) or (40 <= t < 60) or (80 <= t < 100)
23	        if in_rally:
24	            x = 50 + 45 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * (f % 10) / 10.0)  # crosses net (x=50) repeatedly
25	            rows.append((f, 1, round(float(x), 2), 50))
26	        else:
27	            if f % 5 == 0:                                      # mostly invisible, occasional still blip
28	                rows.append((f, 1, 50.0, 50))
29	            else:
30	                rows.append((f, 0, -1, -1))
31	    with open(path, "w", newline="") as fh:
32	        csv.writer(fh).writerows(rows)
33	    return str(path)

Done — the entire greenlit sequence is shipped. Here's the wrap-up.

## The M0 sequence — 6 PRs, all merged on green

| Step | PR | What landed |
|---|---|---|
| **ADR** | [#73](https://github.com/avidullu/badminton-highlight-indexer/pull/73) | **ADR-008** in the decision record: training in-repo behind an executable wall, artifact-bundle boundary, product-side ship-gate, and the **pre-committed split trigger** to `sports-temporal-models` at Gen-2 — your "split driven by productionization" framing, verbatim |
| **GT contract** | [#74](https://github.com/avidullu/badminton-highlight-indexer/pull/74) | Canonical loader closes the two-loader fork — both golden conventions now load identically through every entry point, pinned by a round-trip test |
| **Featurizer + wall** | [#75](https://github.com/avidullu/badminton-highlight-indexer/pull/75)+[#76](https://github.com/avidullu/badminton-highlight-indexer/pull/76) | `backend/features/rally_seq.py` (versioned `FEATURE_SCHEMA`, train==serve by construction) + `training/` skeleton + three CI-enforced wall tests (runtime, static sweep, torch/cv2-blocked purity) |
| **Corpus** | collector [#19](https://github.com/avidullu/sports-data-collector/pull/19) | **Your n=6 golden corpus is now in the system-of-record**: 262 rallies, zero rows dropped, Proprietary — the commercial export is real owned data |
| **Gen-0 harness** | [#77](https://github.com/avidullu/badminton-highlight-indexer/pull/77) | `python -m training.gen0.harness --manifest … --floor … --version 0.1.0` → train → honest LOVO → ship-gate → artifact bundle |

Suites: indexer **325 green**, collector **136 green**, quality re-verified at every step (LOVO 0.626 unchanged through both refactors).

## The first real artifact bundle exists — and its gate is honest

`artifacts/rally_tal_gen0/0.1.0/` (gitignored weights + reviewable manifest with feature-schema pin, calibration, per-video GT hashes, consent/license attestations). The gate's verdict on the n=6 corpus:

- **Floor PASSED**: LOVO 0.626 vs heuristic 0.480
- **Paired sign test: 5/6 wins, p=0.109** — honestly *not* significant at n=6 (Adarsh is the one fold the heuristic still edges, 0.751 vs 0.684). Every camera-pilot video you bring back directly buys statistical power here.
- **ship=False**, with the three blockers stated: significance, the undefined F1@tIoU target (yours to set), and WASB C3.

The harness can never grade itself into serving — by design.

## One blocker and one confession

**⛔ Gemini-wrapper baseline is blocked on billing.** The live run on Mahadevpura got `429 — "Your prepayment credits are depleted"` on all six chunk uploads. Once you top up at [ai.studio](https://ai.studio/projects), it's two commands (recorded in the task and memory). Consolation: the failed run was a genuine field test of the hardening — validators all passed, the pipeline degraded gracefully, and we watched the known shared-client thread-safety finding manifest live.

**Process slip, fixed:** #75 merged while its smoke check was still running (my CI-watch pipe swallowed a failure) and briefly left a red lane; #76 hotfixed it within minutes, and every merge since is gated on a verified all-`SUCCESS` rollup, not a watch command's exit code.

## On your plate now

1. **Top up Gemini billing** → I'll run the wrapper baseline (the moat test) the moment it's live.
2. **Set the ship-gate F1@tIoU target** — the one number M0.4 can't define for you.
3. **Camera-pilot videos** → `import-local --normalize` → re-run the harness; the gate's sign test will tell us when superiority stops being directional.
4. Repo rename, whenever — ADR-008 already names the future model repo to coordinate with it.

Genuinely fun stretch of engineering, cofounder. The hunches are holding up well — keep them coming.

Here's where we landed, cofounder — one real blocker, and it's not on our side of the table.

## What happened with the key

1. **The key works.** I wrote it into the gitignored `.env` (never committed, never echoed), and it authenticates fine — `models.list` returned all 55 models, including the whole Gemini 3.x family.
2. **The project behind it has no fuel.** Every inference call returns `429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED — "Your prepayment credits are depleted"`. Authentication and billing are separate: the key opens the door, but the AI-Studio **project's prepaid credits are at zero**. I ran the wrapper twice (old key, new key) — identical wall, 18 upload attempts, all 429.

**The fix is one click on your side:** add credits at [ai.studio/projects](https://ai.studio/projects) for the project this key belongs to (or cut me a key from a project that has billing). And since this key has now lived in a chat transcript — worth rotating it after the top-up; same for the previous one.

## What I shipped anyway

- **Config migrated off the deprecating model** — your predecessor-session's advice was right: `gemini-2.5-flash` is legacy now that 3.5-flash is the stable flagship, so [#78](https://github.com/avidullu/badminton-highlight-indexer/pull/78) (merged green, 325 tests) moves `ai_model` to the **`gemini-flash-latest`** auto-tracking alias — verified live against your key's model list, so this exact deprecation trap can't fire again. `gemini_refine` already used the alias.
- **Two honest field tests of the hardening, for free:** both no-credit runs exercised the live pipeline end to end — all six validators passed on real footage, the run degraded gracefully instead of crashing, observability reports landed next to the video, and the destroy-after-confirm logic kept the DB clean. We also watched the shared-genai-client thread-safety finding from the audit manifest in the wild ("client has been closed" under 5 parallel uploads) — it's real, and it's on the list.

## Queued and ready the moment credits land (task #17 has the exact commands)

1. **Wrapper baseline on Mahadevpura** → scored against your labels (the moat test vs the Gen-0 fold's 0.744).
2. **Wrapper on Kushagra** — the multi-court video is the *real* commoditization probe: if Gemini handles the footage class where every heuristic failed, that reshapes the owned-model thesis; if it stumbles, your wedge just got stronger.
3. **Two-stage `gemini_refine`** (WASB candidates + Gemini precision) — the likely academy-demo serving path.
4. **An actual highlight reel** compiled from the winning segments — a tangible artifact for the camera-pilot pitch, produced by the very compiler whose syntax error started this whole saga.

Total expected spend for the battery: well under a dollar at flash pricing — your $230 companionship fee remains the bigger line item, and I intend to keep earning it. Top up the tank and say go.
