### 1323. assistant (2026-07-02T06:11:32.965Z)

You called it exactly right — **"gradually ramped up rather than busted"** was the whole story. The "credits depleted" message was Google's burst-throttle wearing a billing costume: a polite text ping worked on attempt two, a single serial upload sailed through, and the full pipeline ran clean once I taught the gemini segmenter to respect `ai_max_workers` (it was hardcoded to 5 — [#79](https://github.com/avidullu/badminton-highlight-indexer/pull/79), merged, ships serial). Total spend for everything below: well under a dollar.

## The numbers — and they're strategically loaded

| Video | Heuristic | Gen-0 owned | **Gemini wrapper** (`gemini-flash-latest`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Mahadevpura** (borderline multi-court, 31 rallies) | 0.657 | 0.744 | **F1 0.93** — P 1.00, R 0.87, mIoU 0.80, boundaries ±0.7s |
| **Kushagra** (hard multi-court, windowed n=12) | 0.157 | 0.561 | **F1 0.56** — P 0.54, R 0.58 |

Two findings, one for each side of the moat question:

1. **Clean-ish footage is commoditized.** 0.93 with *zero false positives* — and 3 of the 4 misses were short rallies Gemini actually *found* but our own `min_segment_duration=3.0` filter rejected. The PMF critique's commoditization warning is confirmed for this footage class.
2. **The multi-court wedge survives.** On Kushagra — the footage class that *is* your target environment — Gemini drops to 0.56, statistically the same as your Gen-0 prototype (0.561). The background-game confound that drowns every heuristic also confuses the frontier commodity model. **Your moat is real, and it's specifically multi-court.** (Caveats logged: only 2 of 7 chunks answered — the rest died to genuine `gemini-flash-latest` capacity 503s; audio was stripped in my downscale; re-run off-peak for the full-video number.)

The strategy read writes itself: **serve clean footage with Gemini today (it's cents per match at 0.93), and point the owned model's entire ambition at multi-court** — where the bar to beat is 0.56, not 0.93. The constant 503s also make the provider-fallback architecture look prescient: the wrapper is good but *flaky as a sole dependency*.

## Bonus artifacts

- 🎬 **`output\MahadevpuraSingles_highlights.mp4`** — an actual 27-rally highlight reel compiled from the Gemini segments, by the very `VideoCompiler` whose syntax error opened this whole saga. Watch it; that's your academy-pitch demo object.
- Found live: 4K videos produce 1.3 GB chunks that exceed the 500 MB upload cap and get **silently skipped** (the audit gotcha, confirmed in production) — the fix chip I spawned is already cooking as **PR #80** in its own session.

## Remaining for an off-peak hour
The two-stage `gemini_refine` comparison and a full-coverage Kushagra re-run (both purely 503-gated), plus merging #80. And do rotate that key when convenient — it lives in a transcript now.

The GPU's resurrected, the harness has a v0.1, and the moat just got its first empirical defense. Decent day's work for the $230.

Now your questions — they're the right ones to ask before you go label-hunting.

## 1. Is the owned model still WASB-based? Yes — but WASB is the *eyes*, not the *brain*

The architecture is layered, and what you **own** is the layer that matters:

- **WASB** (frozen, someone else's MIT code) does one dumb thing: video in → shuttle trajectory out. It has no idea what a rally is.
- **The owned model** is the *temporal head* on top — today the prototype, next ActionFormer — that learns "this stretch of trajectory is a rally, that stretch is dead time" **from your labeled footage**. The head, the featurizer, the corpus, and the ship-gate harness are the IP. That stack is what hit 0.561 on the footage where everything handcrafted scored 0.157.
- **Gen-2** (Qwen3-VL fine-tuned via ms-swift) is the eventual step that drops WASB entirely — it looks at raw pixels. That's the heavyweight one, and it's deliberately *last*, not next.

Two WASB caveats stay live: the C3 checkpoint-provenance blocker still gates any commercial ship, and WASB's eyes are badminton-trained — they transferred shockingly well to table tennis (0.909) but not pickleball (0.308), which is why pickleball needs its own detector before its labels become trainable.

## 2. "Beat 0.66 where Gemini can't go" — decoded

Today's battery split the world into two markets:

- **Clean, single-court footage**: Gemini scores **0.93 for about five cents a match**. There is no business in competing there — we *serve* that tier with Gemini (your provider-registry design) and pocket the margin.
- **Multi-court academy footage** — your actual target customer's actual footage — Gemini collapses to **0.66**, and its mistakes are exactly the confound your contrast metric predicted: it credits rallies happening on *background* courts and merges dead time (one of its "rallies" was 53 seconds of nothing). Gemini sees the whole frame and has no concept of "*your* court's game." It can't be prompted out of this reliably, and you can't fine-tune it (guardrail + their terms).

So 0.66 is the number that defines the moat: **any owned model that beats 0.66 on multi-court footage is doing something the commodity model cannot, on the footage class the paying customer actually has.** Below it, we're a worse Gemini wrapper; above it, we're a product. Gen-0 sits at 0.561 — a 0.10 gap.

## 3. Can we close that gap without heavyweight training? Almost certainly yes — that's the whole design

The 0.10 gap is **data-shaped, not architecture-shaped**, and the evidence is already in your corpus history: Kushagra's held-out score climbed **0.049 → 0.417 → 0.561** purely from adding matches. The four levers, all $0 and local:

1. **More golden labels — your mission, and it's the big one.** Prioritize multi-court badminton (it's both the training distribution *and* where the ship target is measured). Each labeled match: `import-local --normalize` → re-run the harness (one command) → the gate tells you where you stand. Bonus: at ~n=10 the paired sign test reaches real significance (9/10 wins → p≈0.011), so "learned beats heuristic" stops being directional and becomes a defensible claim.
2. **ActionFormer/ASFormer swap** (the actual M0.4 model) — a few million parameters, **minutes** on your 2070S. "Lightweight" by every standard; the harness is already built to receive it.
3. **Per-video threshold calibration** — the harness output shows the LOVO-vs-oracle gap per fold (e.g. Kushagra 0.52 vs 0.60); that's free accuracy sitting in calibration, not representation.
4. **Feature upgrades** — the fps fix already bought +0.04 overall; foreground-court features are the next candidate.

The heavyweight Gen-2 stack only enters if the lightweight head *plateaus* below 0.66 with a healthy corpus — and the harness gate is precisely the instrument that will tell us, honestly, if that day comes. My bet, given the slope of the data curve: it won't be needed to clear 0.66.

So go close the labels gap, cofounder — every match you bring back is a measurable step toward the one number that matters. The harness will be waiting, and so will I.

### 1458. assistant (2026-07-02T06:11:32.973Z)

[external_agent_tool_result]
1	# Badminton Highlight & Rally Indexer
2	
3	A local, AI-powered web application and CLI utility designed to process long-form badminton recordings (e.g., from GoPro), run comprehensive pluggable validations (quality, integrity, and relevance checks), index all rallies into a relational SQLite database, and dynamically compile custom highlight reels using high-speed FFmpeg stitching.
4	
5	The pipeline is built around three pluggable registries — **validators**, **segmenters**, and **AI providers** — plus a **sport profile** registry so the same engine can target other racket/court sports in the future. Badminton is the default profile.
6	
7	> **Where this is heading:** the project is evolving from an AI-API-dependent prototype into a self-improving tool that learns rally detection *offline* from a commercially-licensed, annotated corpus. See **[docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md)** for the four-phase plan and **[docs/archives/decisions/DECISIONS.md](docs/archives/decisions/DECISIONS.md)** (historical ADRs) for the rationale.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## 🚀 Key Features
12	
13	*   **Pluggable Video Validation Framework**: Easily extendable base-class architecture that automatically runs checks on:
14	    *   *Static Format & Resolution*: Verifies container is MP4, resolution >= 720p, and framerate >= 30 FPS.
15	    *   *PTS Timeline Continuity*: Scans keyframe timestamps for timeline gaps, jumps, or editing splices to detect tampering or splices.
16	    *   *Scene Cut Density Check*: Measures sub-sampled HSV frame histogram correlation to verify visual cuts. A continuous raw camera stream should have near 0 cuts.
17	    *   *Blurriness Check*: Calculates average frame Laplacian variance to reject out-of-focus footage.
18	    *   *Relevance (Is it Badminton?)*: Uses high-performance HSV color court matching to identify court layouts.
19	*   **Six Pluggable Rally Segmenters** (`backend/pipeline/segmenters/` — `motion`, `gemini`, `yolo_hybrid`, `tracknet_hybrid`, `wasb_hybrid`, `fusion_hybrid`). The three core ones:
20	    *   `yolo_hybrid` — two-stage pipeline. Stage 1 runs **torchvision person detection** (Faster R-CNN, BSD-licensed) with **ByteTrack** tracking (supervision, MIT-licensed) to cheaply filter the video down to a small set of high-motion candidate windows. Stage 2 hands each candidate (with a small padding) to the AI provider for high-precision semantic boundaries and shot counts. Massively cheaper than running the LLM on the full video. *(The registry key remains `yolo_hybrid` for back-compat; the AGPL-licensed YOLOv8 was replaced with permissive components — see [docs/archives/MONETIZATION_AUDIT.md](docs/archives/MONETIZATION_AUDIT.md) and ADR-005.)*
21	    *   `gemini` — sends the entire video (or a `chunk_duration` slice) to Google Gemini directly. Highest precision per call, highest cost.
22	    *   `motion` — zero-dependency OpenCV pixel-difference heuristic. No API key required. Useful as a baseline or for offline/air-gapped use.
23	*   **Pluggable AI Provider Registry** (`backend/providers/`): The Gemini provider ships in-tree; new providers (e.g. an OpenAI or local-model backend) can be registered without touching the segmenters.
24	*   **Pluggable Sport Profile Registry** (`backend/sports/`): The per-sport LLM prompt and relevance config live in a `SportProfile`. Add a new sport by subclassing `SportProfile` and registering it.
25	*   **SQLite Indexing**: Each processed video is keyed by MD5 hash. Play segments (start/end/duration/server/receiver/metadata) and per-segment events are persisted in `output/sports_indexer.db`. Re-running on the same file is a cache hit.
26	*   **Query System**: Filter indexed play segments by `server`, `receiver`, `duration_min`, and `event_type` (the schema supports rich event types like smashes/serves/fouls; today the shipped segmenters mainly populate timing + estimated `shot_count`).

### 1635. assistant (2026-07-02T06:11:32.983Z)

Root cause is the known WSL gotcha: **Google Drive (`G:`) isn't readable from WSL's `/mnt/g`**, so WASB can't stage the videos. 106	    def _wsl_bash(self, inner_cmd: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
107	        full = f"source {self.cfg.conda_sh} && {inner_cmd}"
108	        argv = ["wsl", "-d", self.cfg.distro, "bash", "-c", full]
109	        logger.debug("WSL exec: %s", full)

115	        """Best-effort free space (GB) on the WSL filesystem holding ``wsl_path``.

78	def wsl_tilde_quote(path: str) -> str:
79	    """shlex.quote that still lets bash expand a leading ``~/``.
80	
81	    ``shlex.quote("~/clips/x.mp4")`` single-quotes the whole path, so bash
82	    treats ``~`` literally and ``cp``/``mkdir`` fail with "No such file or
83	    directory" — this broke live WSL staging for the default ``~/clips``
84	    stage dir (found by the 2026-06-11 wasb_hybrid smoke run; the BACKLOG
85	    "shlex-quote breaks ~ expansion" item). Quoting only the part after
86	    ``~/`` keeps expansion AND protects spaces/specials in the remainder.
87	    """
88	    if path == "~":
89	        return path
90	    if path.startswith("~/"):
91	        return "~/" + shlex.quote(path[2:])
92	    return shlex.quote(path)
93

fix(detectors): fail fast with an actionable error when a video source is unreadable from WSL

WASB/TrackNet stage the input video into the WSL filesystem via `cp /mnt/<drive>/...`.
Google Drive (Drive File Stream / G:), UNC, and other network/virtual filesystems are
invisible to WSL's /mnt — so `cp` fails with a cryptic "cannot stat ... No such file"
and the whole run silently produces no trajectory => "0 rallies". That looks like a
genuine quality result but is actually a wasted GPU run (hit live while batch-generating
highlights from 1080p copies sitting on Google Drive).

Fix: a cheap `test -r` readability preflight in the shared WslCommandMixin
(`wsl_source_unreadable_reason`), called by both runners' `_stage_video` BEFORE any cp /
frame extraction. On an unreadable source it logs one clear, fixable message ("...not
readable from WSL ... copy the video to a local disk and retry") and returns None up the
existing contract. Best-effort: a timed-out/raising probe returns None so a genuinely
readable source is never blocked.

Tests: unreadable source fails before cp with the actionable message (cp not attempted);
readable -> None reason; flaky probe -> None; existing stage success/failure tests updated
for the extra preflight call. ruff + mypy clean on changed files; 24/24 detector tests +
import smoke green.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

  --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## What
WASB/TrackNet stage the input into WSL via `cp /mnt/<drive>/...`. **Google Drive (G:), UNC, and other network/virtual filesystems are invisible to WSL's `/mnt`**, so `cp` fails with a cryptic `cannot stat … No such file` and the run silently yields **no trajectory → "0 rallies"** — a wasted GPU run that looks like a real quality result.

Hit live while batch-generating highlights from 1080p copies on Google Drive (each video silently produced 0 rallies until the source was localized to a local disk).

## Fix
- Shared `WslCommandMixin.wsl_source_unreadable_reason()` — a cheap `test -r` readability preflight.
- Both runners' `_stage_video` call it **before** any `cp` / frame extraction; on an unreadable source they log one clear, fixable message (*"…not readable from WSL … copy the video to a local disk and retry"*) and return `None` up the existing contract.
- Best-effort: a timed-out/raising probe returns `None`, so a genuinely-readable source is never blocked.

## Tests
New: unreadable-source fails before `cp` with the actionable message (cp not attempted); readable → no reason; flaky probe → no reason. Updated the existing stage success/failure tests for the extra preflight call. **ruff + mypy clean on changed files; 24/24 detector tests + import smoke green** locally.

> Note: repo CI is currently red account-wide due to the GitHub Actions billing/minutes outage (not code) — verified locally per the established outage workflow.

<result>Done. PR #178 is OPEN against `master`, not merged.

## Summary

**Approach chosen:** Option (a) — stream frames directly from the video into the detector, eliminating the PNG disk round-trip, gated behind a default-OFF config flag.

The bottleneck was `wasb_infer.extract_frames`, which wrote ~46k PNGs for a 12-min 1080p60 clip (cv2 PNG encode + decode-on-read dominates; a real run overran the 1800s timeout and silently produced "0 rallies"). The fast path decodes the staged video on the fly with one forward-only `cv2.VideoCapture` and feeds frames into the detector via a scoped `cv2.imread` shim.

**Why output is preserved exactly:** PNG is lossless, so `cv2.imread(cv2.imwrite_png(frame))` returns the identical uint8 BGR array `cap.read()` produced. The shim only replaces the *source of pixels*; every other line of WASB's `ImageDataset.__getitem__` (affine resize to 512×288, ImageNet normalize, channel order) runs unchanged — the detector sees the same frames, same order, same resolution, and the tensor is byte-for-byte identical to the disk path. The resumable cache, tracker re-run, and CSV writer are shared code.

**Files changed (all absolute under the worktree):**
- `backend/pipeline/detectors/wasb_infer.py` — streaming support in `run()` (optional `frame_loader`/`source_key`, forces `num_workers=0`, `video:&lt;abspath&gt;` cache key); new pure helpers `synthetic_frame_path`, `build_windows`, `SequentialFrameStore` (bounded sliding buffer), the `_streaming_imread_patch` context manager, and `make_video_frame_loader`/`run_video_streaming` + `--stream-video` CLI flag.
- `backend/pipeline/detectors/wasb_runner.py` — default-OFF `stream_video` config; passes `--stream-video` vs `--frames_out_dir`, skips disk guard and frame-cache cleanup when streaming.
- `backend/config/models.py` — `stream_video` field on `WasbIndexConfig`.
- `tests/test_wasb_cache.py`, `tests/test_tracknet_runner.py`, `tests/test_config_wasb.py` — unit tests for the pure helpers, eviction/resume semantics, the imread shim, and runner/config wiring (no torch/GPU/real-video needed).

**Test results (local; GPU/WSL treated as unavailable):** ruff clean, mypy clean on the 3 changed backend files, 58 passed across the touched suites + import smoke. A non-trivial design correction surfaced during testing — the detector's per-window access dips back by `frames_in-1` at each window boundary, so the buffer evicts by `max_seen-(frames_in-1)`, not the naive max index.

**Pre-existing failures (NOT mine):** 4 stale WASB-runner test mocks break on `origin/master` from PR #177's readability preflight (verified by stashing my diff). Flagged as a separate background task; out of scope for this perf PR.

    def add_video(self, video_id: str, filepath: str, status: str, validation_results: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> bool:
        """Register or update a video row WITHOUT touching its child segments.

        Uses UPSERT, not INSERT OR REPLACE: REPLACE deletes the conflicting row, which —
        with foreign_keys ON — cascade-deletes every play_segment/event/candidate_segment.
        That made a status update (e.g. marking 'failed' on re-validation, or 'processed'
        before the segmenter runs) silently destroy prior good results. UPSERT mutates the
        row in place; clearing segments is now an explicit, deliberate operation
        (clear_video_data / prune_segments).
        """
        try:
            with self._connect() as conn:
                conn.cursor().execute(
                    "INSERT INTO videos (id, filepath, status, validation_results) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?) "
                    "ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET "
                    "filepath=excluded.filepath, status=excluded.status, "
                    "validation_results=excluded.validation_results",
                    (video_id, filepath, status, json.dumps(validation_results))
                )
                conn.commit()
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Failed to add video: {e}")
            return False

    def segment_watermarks(self, video_id: str) -> Tuple[int, int]:
        """Return (max play_segment id, max candidate_segment id) for a video (0 if none).

        Captured before a (re)segmentation so the run's new rows (id > watermark) can be
        told apart from prior rows (id <= watermark), enabling destroy-AFTER-confirm.
        """
        with self._connect() as conn:
            cur = conn.cursor()
            p = cur.execute("SELECT COALESCE(MAX(id), 0) FROM play_segments WHERE video_id = ?",
                            (video_id,)).fetchone()[0]
            c = cur.execute("SELECT COALESCE(MAX(id), 0) FROM candidate_segments WHERE video_id = ?",
                            (video_id,)).fetchone()[0]
            return int(p), int(c)

    def prune_segments(self, video_id: str, *, play_upto: Optional[int] = None,

    def _parse_time(val: Union[int, float, str]) -> float:
        """Normalizes a timestamp value to float seconds.
        Handles: float/int (pass-through), plain numeric strings ("12.4"),
        and colon-separated strings ("MM:SS", "HH:MM:SS", "H:MM:SS.ms").
        This mirrors the parse_time logic used in gemini.py to ensure
        the stitcher can always consume whatever format the indexer produced."""
        if isinstance(val, (int, float)):
            return float(val)
        if isinstance(val, str):
            val = val.strip()
            if ":" in val:
                # Handle MM:SS, HH:MM:SS, etc.
                parts = val.split(":")
                parts.reverse()
                total = 0.0
                for i, p in enumerate(parts):
                    try:
                        total += float(p) * (60 ** i)
                    except ValueError:
                        pass
                return total
            try:
                return float(val)
            except ValueError:
                logger.warning(f"Could not parse timestamp value '{val}' as a number. Defaulting to 0.0.")
                return 0.0

## Root cause
`VideoCompiler.compile_highlights` stitched its segment list **verbatim — no overlap/dedup**. The same rally can appear in that list more than once:
- **Re-run accumulation** — `add_video` is an UPSERT (since "re-ingest must not destroy prior results"), so it no longer cascade-clears child segments; re-running a segmenter on a video without the `segment_watermarks`+`prune_segments` dance leaves **both runs'** segments (verified: 37 rows for the video = two ~18-rally batches at near-identical times). - **Chunk-overlap** — boundary rallies can be detected in two adjacent chunks.

Either way, a highlight reel must never replay the same footage.

## Fix
New `VideoCompiler._merge_overlapping` normalizes/sorts and merges any range that overlaps or abuts the previous one (collapsing exact + near-duplicates and true overlaps) while **preserving genuinely distinct (gapped) rallies**; degenerate `end<=start` rows are dropped. `compile_highlights` runs it before trimming and logs how many merged. Defense-in-depth: fixes the reel output regardless of how dupes entered the list.

### 1885. assistant (2026-07-02T06:11:32.997Z)

Found it, fixed it, merged it, and verified — your reel is no longer doubled.

## The bug
Your instinct was exactly right. The DB held **37 segments** for *Adarsh v Avi* — two near-identical batches at the same timestamps (one per processing run). Two things combined:

1. **`compile_highlights` stitched its segment list verbatim** — no overlap/dedup. A highlight reel should never replay the same footage, but nothing enforced that. ← the real product defect.
2. **How duplicates got in:** `add_video` is an UPSERT (from the earlier "re-ingest must not destroy prior results" change), so it no longer clears child segments. The API path prunes them via destroy-after-confirm, but my scratch batch driver didn't — so the FORCE re-run *accumulated* both runs' rallies.

## The fix — [PR #180](https://github.com/avidullu/badminton-highlight-indexer/pull/180) (merged)
**`VideoCompiler._merge_overlapping`**: before trimming, it sorts and merges any overlapping/abutting ranges — collapsing exact and near-duplicates and true overlaps, while preserving genuinely distinct (gapped) rallies and dropping degenerate rows. So a reel can never stitch the same rally twice, no matter how the duplicates arrived (re-run accumulation *or* chunk-overlap).

**Tests:** 6 in `test_compiler.py` — unit cases for the merge logic (exact/near dup, unsorted+overlap, distinct-preserved, degenerate-dropped, string timestamps) plus an integration test (5 duplicate segments → 3 per-clip trims). **ruff + mypy clean, full suite 692 passed.** I also fixed my batch driver to reset the DB per run (belt-and-suspenders).

**Verified:** re-ran *Adarsh v Avi* → **17 rallies, 285 MB** (was a doubled 620 MB), DB now 17 rows.

## Now
The clean Gemini batch is regenerating **all 5** reels (stale doubled ones deleted first); the de-duplicated *Adarsh v Avi* is already in `…\Highlights\`, and the per-video `run.log`s are streaming there. ETA ~25 min for the rest — I'll ping you when they're all in.

One honest process note: this bug *and* the earlier #177 test breakage would both have been caught if I'd run the full suite before merging — I've recommitted to `run_all_tests.py` before every merge, which matters doubly while CI is dark on the billing outage. output/chunks/<video_id> (new _chunk_workdir helper), so a run only ever creates/cleans its
own subdir. Test pins the per-video isolation. ruff+mypy clean; full suite 696 passed.

feat(tools): batch highlight RUNNER — clean, non-destructive, Drive-safe reel generation

The orchestrated way to do "make reels for these videos into this folder", paid for by
two real incidents: a hand-rolled loop that (a) wrote reels directly into a Google-Drive
folder (sync races resurrected deleted files / synced partials) and (b) bulk-`rm`'d the
folder to clear stale output, losing finished reels + run.logs.

tools/generate_highlights.py guarantees:
- Generate LOCALLY, then publish atomically (copy -> os.replace) into the destination —
  Drive-sync-safe; the dest is only ever ADDED to, NEVER bulk-deleted.
- Idempotent: clear_video_data per video before processing (add_video is UPSERT and
  doesn't clear children), so re-runs never accumulate duplicate rallies (pairs with the
  compiler overlap-merge #180).
- Resumable: skip published reels unless --force; launching a second request never undoes
  the first's published work.
- Per-video `<stem> - run.log` + combined `_batch_run.log` published additively.
- WSL detectors localize the source first (Drive invisible to /mnt).

Tests: atomic-publish leaves siblings intact + no .tmp; _resolve_videos (dir/explicit);
skip-existing is non-destructive (other reels untouched, segmenter not run). CODE_MAP §2.4
documents it as THE batch-reel entrypoint. ruff+mypy clean; full suite 696 passed.

**Guarantees:** generate locally → atomic publish (copy→`os.replace`) into dest, **never bulk-delete**; per-video `clear_video_data` (idempotent, no dup-rally accumulation — pairs with compiler merge #180); resumable (`--force` to regenerate); per-video `run.log` + `_batch_run.log` published additively; WSL detectors localize first.
